findings.title: Fallback result depends on per-site default_locale, but the process-wide translation cache key ignores it
findings.body:
`FallbackLocaleList#[]` makes the result of a lookup depend on `SiteSetting.default_locale`. That value differs per site in multisite and can be changed at runtime.

The LRU cache in `lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb` is process-global. Its key is `"#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}"`, which does not include the site's default locale or the fallback chain.

Example: a key missing in `fr` is first resolved on a site whose default is `de`. The German string is cached under the `fr` key. It is then returned to `fr` users on every other site in the same process, including a site whose default is `es`. Changing `default_locale` on a single site also leaves stale fallback strings in the cache.

Fix: include the fallback chain (or `SiteSetting.default_locale`) in the cache key, or clear the cache when it changes.

findings.title: Fallback locales are only loaded in the controller before_filter, so fallbacks fail outside web requests
findings.body:
The lazy-loading patch's `I18n.translate` only calls `load_locale(config.locale)`. The fallback locales (site default and `:en`) are loaded only by `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!`, and that is called only from `ApplicationController#set_locale`.

That call is skipped in several places:
- Sidekiq jobs and mailers that switch `I18n.locale` to a user's locale.
- Rake tasks and middleware.
- Controllers that skip `set_locale`.
- Calls that pass an explicit `locale:` option.

In all of these, the fallback locales may not be loaded in that process. A key missing in the user's locale then produces a 'translation missing' string instead of the site-default or English text. For argument-less lookups, that missing-translation result is also frozen into the LRU cache.

Fallback loading belongs in `translate`/`load_locale` itself, e.g. by loading every locale in `I18n.fallbacks[locale]`.
